mainTopic: Whether היסח הדעת is a פסול טומאה or פסול הגוף, and the רבנן's extra stringency (מעלה) for holy things regarding השקה and זריעה
overview: This amud has three discussions. First, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue whether היסח הדעת, diverting attention from guarding קדשים, is a פסול טומאה or a פסול הגוף. A ברייתא saying only body defects are burned right away is answered: its author requires עיבור צורה even for פיגול. A second ברייתא says an offering is accepted after the fact, which seems to work only if the ציץ atones for a טומאה problem. ריש לקיש answers that 'disqualified' there means touched by a טבול יום, a second kind of טומאה. Next, רבי ירמיה rejects a Babylonian explanation of planted impure תרומה. He uses רבי אושעיא's ruling on impure water for סוכות to show that זריעה does not work for הקדש or for תרומה. אביי asks whether this stringency applies to things made holy only by speech. רב דימי brings a parallel case of impure grapes, but רב יוסף rejects the proof, and the גמרא reconciles two rulings of רבי יוחנן about pressing impure grapes. Finally, רבא begins a proof from the פרה אדומה water. He points to a tension in the פסוק, and the argument continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא's rule: a body defect is burned at once, other defects wait
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה is quoted as a challenge to ריש לקיש. A defect in the body of the offering means it is burned immediately. A defect in the blood or in the owners means it waits for עיבור צורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any offering whose problem is in its own body is burned right away. If the problem is in the blood or in the owners, we wait until its form decays, and then it goes out to the place of burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a ברייתא that רבי יוחנן is using to challenge ריש לקיש. The ברייתא sorts disqualified offerings into two groups: burn right away, or wait first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives a clear rule: only a פסול הגוף is burned immediately. In the ברייתא, the case connected to היסח הדעת is treated as one that waits for עיבור צורה. That suggests היסח הדעת is not a פסול הגוף, which is exactly what ריש לקיש claimed.

keyTerms.meaning: Its disqualification is in its body, meaning the meat itself is defective
It is burned immediately
The owners of the offering
Letting the meat sit overnight until its appearance changes before burning it
The designated place where disqualified קדשים are burned

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think עיבור צורה means the meat is still kosher. In both groups the meat ends up burned. The only question is whether we burn it right away or wait for it to spoil first.

phrases.english: Anything whose disqualification is in its body
is burned immediately.
If the problem is in the blood or in the owners,
their form must decay first,
and then they go out to the place of burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted on the previous amud as a challenge to ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that היסח הדעת is a פסול הגוף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only a פסול הגוף is burned immediately, and היסח הדעת is not burned immediately, then היסח הדעת cannot be a פסול הגוף.

steps.title: This תנא requires waiting even for פיגול
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that this תנא follows the תנא of דבי רבה בר אבוה, who requires עיבור צורה even for פיגול. So waiting proves nothing about whether a defect is a פסול הגוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to him: This תנא is the תנא of the school of רבה בר אבוה, who says that even פיגול needs its form to decay first.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש defends himself. He says this ברייתא follows a view where even a clear body defect like פיגול must wait before burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's proof assumed that 'waiting' means 'not a body defect.' ריש לקיש shows that for this תנא, even פיגול, a classic פסול הגוף, waits for עיבור צורה. So the fact that the case waits tells us nothing, and the challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: This תנא, the author of the ברייתא
Of the school of רבה בר אבוה
An offering ruined by an improper intention during its service, an obvious body defect
Requires

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא: a source that seems to prove a point is neutralized by showing that its author holds a different underlying view.

phrases.english: He said to him: This תנא

phrases.aramaic: תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ הוּא,
phrases.english: is the תנא of the school of רבה בר אבוה,
who says: Even פיגול
requires decay of form.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַאי תַּנָּא, תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a specific תנא with a broader rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Waiting for עיבור צורה shows that a defect is not a פסול הגוף.
steps.terutzMaskana: For this תנא, even a פסול הגוף like פיגול waits, so the ברייתא proves nothing against ריש לקיש.

steps.title: A new ברייתא: blood thrown for disqualified meat is accepted
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings a second ברייתא. If the meat became impure, disqualified, or left the קלעים, רבי אליעזר says to throw the blood and רבי יהושע says not to. Still, רבי יהושע agrees that if the blood was thrown, the offering is accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: If the meat became impure, or became disqualified, or went outside the curtains, רבי אליעזר says the blood is thrown, and רבי יהושע says it is not thrown. But רבי יהושע agrees that if it was thrown, the offering is accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן quotes another ברייתא against ריש לקיש. This step only sets up the source; the actual argument comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists three problems with the meat: טומאה, being 'disqualified,' and leaving its boundary. The important line is that even רבי יהושע agrees the offering is accepted after the fact. The challenge will turn on what 'disqualified' means and why the offering could still be accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: Became disqualified
Outside the curtains, meaning outside the area where the meat may be eaten
He should throw the blood on the מזבח
The offering is accepted and has achieved atonement

phrases.english: He challenged him: If the meat became impure or became disqualified,
or it went out beyond the curtains,
רבי אליעזר says: He throws the blood;
רבי יהושע says: He does not throw it.
And רבי יהושע agrees
that if he did throw it, the offering is accepted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a fresh challenge against ריש לקיש after the first one was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that היסח הדעת is a פסול הגוף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup step: the ברייתא will be read as showing that 'disqualified' meat can still be accepted, which fits only a טומאה-type defect.

steps.title: Only the ציץ explains why it is accepted
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן argues that 'disqualified' must mean היסח הדעת. If that is a פסול טומאה, the ציץ atones for it and the offering is accepted. If it is a פסול הגוף, why would it be accepted?
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'disqualified' mean? Doesn't it mean through היסח הדעת? If you say it is a טומאה-type disqualification, that explains how the ציץ can make it accepted. But if you say it is a defect in the body, why is it accepted?
steps.whatsHappening: Here רבי יוחנן makes his argument from the ברייתא. Acceptance after the fact only makes sense if היסח הדעת is a טומאה issue that the ציץ can fix.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Disqualified' cannot mean impure or taken outside, since those are listed separately, so it must mean היסח הדעת. The ציץ atones only for problems of טומאה, not for body defects. Since the ברייתא says the offering is accepted, היסח הדעת must be a פסול טומאה, against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Diverting one's attention from guarding the meat
Disqualifications based on concern about impurity
The כהן גדול's golden frontplate, which atones for טומאה in offerings
Makes the offering accepted, effects atonement
A defect in the item itself

steps.confusionAlert: The ציץ does not fix every problem. It works only for טומאה. That is the entire basis of this challenge.

phrases.english: What does 'disqualified' mean?
Is it not through diverted attention?
It works out well if you say
that it is a טומאה-type disqualification;
that is how you find a case
where the ציץ makes it accepted.
But if you say
it is a defect in the body,
why is it accepted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the ברייתא quoted in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that היסח הדעת is a פסול הגוף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ציץ atones only for טומאה. If the offering is accepted, the defect must be a טומאה defect, not a פסול הגוף.

steps.title: 'Disqualified' means invalidated by a טבול יום
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that 'disqualified' in the ברייתא is not היסח הדעת. It means the meat was touched by a טבול יום, which is a type of טומאה that the ציץ covers.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'disqualified' mean? Disqualified by contact with a טבול יום.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש reinterprets the word 'disqualified' so the ברייתא is not talking about היסח הדעת at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Contact with a טבול יום makes meat invalid, but the meat cannot pass impurity on to other things. Because this is a טומאה-related problem, the ציץ can atone for it. That explains why the offering is accepted without any proof about היסח הדעת.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who has immersed but must wait until nightfall to become fully pure

phrases.english: What does 'disqualified' mean? Disqualified through a טבול יום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case in the ברייתא
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Disqualified' means invalidated by a טבול יום, a טומאה-type problem the ציץ covers.

steps.title: Isn't that the same as 'impure'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a טבול יום case is just טומאה, which the ברייתא already listed as 'impure.' So why mention it a second time?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, that is the same as 'impure'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on ריש לקיש's answer, claiming it makes the ברייתא repeat itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists 'impure' and 'disqualified' as separate cases. If 'disqualified' is also a kind of טומאה, the second item seems unnecessary. That suggests 'disqualified' must mean something else, such as היסח הדעת.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
That is the same as

phrases.english: If so, that is the same as 'impure'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's answer in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's reading of 'disqualified' as טבול יום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא would be listing the same category twice.

steps.title: Two different kinds of impurity
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the ברייתא lists two kinds of טומאה. 'Impure' is meat that can pass impurity on to other things. 'Disqualified' is meat invalidated by a טבול יום, which cannot pass impurity on.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two kinds of impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש: the ברייתא is not repeating itself, because it lists two different levels of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat that is fully טמא can make other things impure. Meat touched by a טבול יום is only פסול and does not spread impurity. Both are covered by the ציץ, so ריש לקיש's position survives the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Two types

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא does not refute ריש לקיש. 'Disqualified' can mean contact with a טבול יום, a weaker form of טומאה that the ציץ covers. So the offering's acceptance proves nothing about היסח הדעת.

phrases.english: There are two kinds of impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy challenge in step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Impure' and 'disqualified by a טבול יום' are the same category.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are two different levels of טומאה: one spreads impurity and one does not.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה rejects the Babylonian explanation
steps.stepSummary: רבין brings רב ששת's teaching to ארץ ישראל. רבי ירמיה rejects it, calling the Babylonians foolish for giving 'dark' explanations.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין went up to ארץ ישראל, he said this teaching before רבי ירמיה. רבי ירמיה said: 'Foolish Babylonians! Because you live in a dark land, you say teachings that are dark and unclear.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the earlier topic of planted impure תרומה. רבי ירמיה rejects the explanation that came from בבל, and this sets up the simpler source he is about to bring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה is not attacking the הלכה itself. He is attacking the way the Babylonians explained it, which he finds needlessly complicated. His next words will give a clearer reason, based on a teaching of the scholars of ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: When he went up (from בבל to ארץ ישראל)
A teaching or halachic statement
Foolish Babylonians
A dark land (בבל, which is low-lying)
That are dark, meaning unclear or murky

steps.confusionAlert: The steps just before this were about רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש and היסח הדעת. This step jumps back to a different, earlier topic on the דף: impure תרומה that was planted. Don't try to connect it to the ציץ discussion.

phrases.english: When Ravin went up (to Eretz Yisrael),
he said this teaching before Rabbi Yirmeya,
phrases.notes: The teaching of רב ששת about planted תרומה.

phrases.english: and he (Rabbi Yirmeya) said: Foolish Babylonians!
Because you live in a dark land,
you say teachings that are dark (unclear).

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי סְלֵיק רָבִין, אַמְרַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתֵּיהּ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the היסח הדעת discussion and returns to the earlier topic of planted impure תרומה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The Babylonian explanation (רב ששת's teaching) of the planted-תרומה case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It is too complicated and unclear, when a simple source already explains the case.

steps.title: The ruling on impure water for the festival
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה quotes ריש לקיש in the name of רבי אושעיא. Impure water for ניסוך המים becomes pure through השקה only if the השקה happens before the water is made holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Haven't you heard what ריש לקיש said in the name of רבי אושעיא? Water for the festival that became impure: if it was touched to a מקוה and only then made holy, it is pure. If it was made holy first and then touched to a מקוה, it is still impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה brings the source that he thinks gives the clear answer. It is a ruling about impure water that was set aside for pouring on the מזבח during סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, impure water becomes pure when it touches the water of a מקוה (השקה). This ruling says the method works only while the water is still ordinary. Once the water is holy, השקה no longer purifies it.

keyTerms.meaning: The water drawn for ניסוך המים, the water-pouring on סוכות
He brought them into contact (with מקוה water)
He made them holy (הקדש)

steps.whyThisMatters: The order of events (השקה first or הקדש first) is the key detail. The next step's proof rests entirely on it.

phrases.english: Have you not heard this

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish in the name of Rabbi Oshaya:
Water of the festival that became impure,
if he touched them (to a mikveh) and afterward consecrated them, they are pure;
if he consecrated them and afterward touched them (to a mikveh), they are impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לְכוּ הָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that רבי ירמיה says the Babylonians missed.
steps.raayaObject: That planting does not remove the status of תרומה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש in the name of רבי אושעיא, on impure מי החג.

steps.title: Planting does not work for holy things or תרומה
steps.stepSummary: Since השקה works like 'planting,' the order should not matter. The fact that it does matter shows that זריעה does not work for הקדש, and the same is true for תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since השקה is like planting, what difference should it make whether the water was touched to the מקוה first or made holy first? This shows that planting does not work for holy things. So here too, planting does not work for תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה draws the lesson from the water ruling and applies it to the planted-תרומה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water touching a מקוה is treated like a seed planted in the ground: it becomes part of the pure source and loses its old status. If that were fully effective, it would work even on holy water. It doesn't, which shows the רבנן were stricter with הקדש. Likewise, planted תרומה keeps its status as תרומה, so it stays forbidden to non-כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Planting: attaching something to a source, like the ground or a מקוה, so it loses its previous status
Since, after all (opens a logical argument)
Evidently, this shows that
The portion of produce given to a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: השקה works like 'planting.' But the רבנן ruled that planting does not undo the status of הקדש, so it also does not undo the status of תרומה. That is why planted תרומה stays forbidden to non-כהנים.

phrases.english: Since it is (like) planting,

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי הִשִּׁיקָן וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִקְדִּישָׁן,
phrases.english: what difference is it to me if he touched them and then consecrated them,

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי הִקְדִּישָׁן וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִשִּׁיקָן?
phrases.english: or if he consecrated them and then touched them?
Evidently, planting is not effective for consecrated items.
Here too, planting is not effective for teruma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general principle from the ruling in step 9 and applies it to תרומה.
steps.raayaObject: Planted impure תרומה keeps its status as תרומה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The difference in order in רבי אושעיא's water ruling.

steps.title: אביי asks how far the stricter rule goes
steps.stepSummary: As רב דימי teaches this ruling, אביי asks whether the stricter rule applies only to water made holy by putting it in a holy vessel, or also to water made holy just by speaking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי sat and taught this ruling. אביי said to him: Was the ruling about water made holy by putting it in a holy vessel? Then if it was made holy just by speaking, the רבנן did not make a stricter rule. Or perhaps the רבנן made a stricter rule even when it was made holy by speaking?
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי repeats רבי אושעיא's ruling, and אביי asks a clarifying question about its scope. This opens the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to make something holy. One is קדושת כלי, placing it in a holy vessel, which is a stronger holiness. The other is קדושת פה, simply declaring it holy. אביי wants to know whether the רבנן's extra strictness (מעלה) applies only to the stronger kind, or to both.

keyTerms.meaning: By placing it in a holy vessel (holiness of the vessel)
By speech, verbally declaring it holy
An extra stringency the רבנן added for holy things
Or perhaps (introduces the second side of a question)

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב דִּימִי וְקָאָמַר לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא.
phrases.english: Rav Dimi sat and was saying this teaching.
Abaye said to him:
Is he speaking of where he consecrated them in a (sacred) vessel,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בַּפֶּה לָא עֲבוּד רַבָּנַן מַעֲלָה.
phrases.english: but by speech the Rabbis did not make a stringency?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא בַּפֶּה נָמֵי עֲבוּד רַבָּנַן מַעֲלָה?
phrases.english: Or perhaps by speech too the Rabbis made a stringency?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב דִּימִי וְקָאָמַר לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא. אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far רבי אושעיא's ruling reaches, now that it has been used as a proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the stricter rule for הקדש apply only to holiness of a vessel, or also to holiness by speech?

steps.title: רב דימי answers with a similar case about impure grapes
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי tells אביי he never heard a ruling on this exact question. He brings a related teaching of רבי יוחנן: impure grapes pressed before הקדש give pure wine, but pressed after הקדש give impure wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I did not hear about this case, but I heard about a similar one. רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: grapes that became impure — if he pressed them and then made them holy, the wine is pure. If he made them holy and then pressed them, the wine is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי admits he has no direct answer to אביי's question. He offers a similar case that may help answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The juice inside an impure grape is normally treated as separate from the grape, so it does not become impure when it comes out. Once the grapes are holy, the רבנן are stricter, and the juice that comes out does become impure. The order of pressing and making holy is what decides the result, just like the order of השקה and הקדש for the water.

keyTerms.meaning: Something similar to it; a parallel case
Grapes that became ritually impure
He pressed (trod on) them
He made them holy (dedicated them to the Temple)

phrases.english: He (Rav Dimi) said to him: This I did not hear,
but I heard something similar to it.
phrases.notes: He offers a parallel case instead of a direct answer.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: For Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Grapes that became impure,
if he pressed them and afterward made them holy, they are pure.
phrases.notes: The wine is pure because the juice inside was treated as separate from the impure grape.

phrases.english: If he made them holy and afterward pressed them, they are impure.
phrases.notes: Extra strictness applies to holy things.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זוֹ לֹא שָׁמַעְתִּי, כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהּ שָׁמַעְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to אביי's question by offering a parallel case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the strictness applies to water made holy only by speech
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no direct tradition, but there is a parallel case: impure grapes pressed after הקדש give impure wine

steps.title: Inference: the Rabbis were strict even with holiness by speech
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that grapes become holy only by speech, yet the רבנן still made a מעלה. So the same should be true for water made holy by speech.
steps.simpleTranslation: But grapes are holy only by speech, and even so the רבנן made a stricter rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from רב דימי's case to answer אביי's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grapes are not made holy by being put in a holy vessel. They become holy only because someone said so. Since the רבנן were still strict with them, it seems that קדושת פה is enough to trigger the מעלה, and that would also apply to the water.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness created by speech alone
An extra stringency made by the רבנן for holy things
And even so

phrases.english: But grapes are things that have holiness by speech only,
and even so, the Rabbis made a stringency.
phrases.notes: This seems to answer אביי: the stricter rule applies even to holiness by speech.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the grapes case to answer אביי's question
steps.raayaObject: The מעלה applies even to things made holy only by speech
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling about impure grapes pressed after הקדש

steps.title: רב יוסף: the grapes case is different
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the grapes case is about תרומה. For תרומה, holiness by speech is the strongest holiness possible, so it counts like holiness by a vessel. Things that need a vessel, like the water, did not get a מעלה when made holy by speech alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: You are talking about grapes? Here we are dealing with grapes of תרומה. For them, holiness by speech is like holiness by a vessel. But for things that need a vessel, the רבנן did not make a stringency when they were made holy only by speech.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף rejects the proof from the grapes case. He shows it does not match the water case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grapes of תרומה never go into a holy vessel, so speech is their full holiness, and that is why the רבנן were strict. Water for ניסוך המים does go into a holy vessel. If it was made holy only by speech, its holiness is not complete, so no מעלה was made. The proof is pushed away, and אביי's question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן
Holiness created by putting something into a holy Temple vessel
We are dealing with
It is comparable to

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף does not say grapes have no holiness. He says that for תרומה, speech is the highest holiness it can get, so it is treated like holiness by a vessel. Water can still get a higher level by going into a vessel.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: You are speaking of grapes?
Here we are dealing with grapes of terumah,

phrases.aramaic: דִּקְדוּשַּׁת פֶּה דִּידְהוּ — כִּקְדוּשַּׁת כְּלִי דָּמְיָא.
phrases.english: whose holiness by speech is like holiness by a vessel.
phrases.notes: Speech is the highest holiness these grapes can have.

phrases.english: But these things that require a vessel,
when made holy by speech, the Rabbis did not make a stringency.
phrases.notes: So the water made holy by speech is not covered by the stricter rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 13
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the grapes case to the water case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: For תרומה, speech is the highest possible holiness and is like vessel holiness. For water, which needs a vessel, speech alone is weaker, so no מעלה was made.
steps.whatToRemember: The grapes case cannot answer אביי. For things that need a holy vessel, the רבנן did not add the מעלה when they were made holy only by speech.

steps.title: Challenge: can one press many impure grapes at once?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's ruling sounds like you can press any amount of grapes. But elsewhere רבי יוחנן says impure grapes must be pressed less than a כביצה at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He pressed them' — even a large amount? Did רבי יוחנן really say that? But רבי יוחנן said: impure grapes should be pressed less than an egg-size at a time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at רבי יוחנן's grape ruling itself and points out a contradiction with another ruling of his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food smaller than a כביצה cannot make other things impure. So pressing small amounts keeps the juice from becoming impure from the grapes. If רבי יוחנן requires that elsewhere, how could he say here, with no limit, that the wine is pure?

keyTerms.meaning: A lot; a large amount
The size of an egg — the minimum amount of food that can pass on impurity
Less and less; small amounts each time

phrases.english: 'He pressed them' — even a large amount?!
Did Rabbi Yochanan really say this?
But Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: עֲנָבִים שֶׁנִּטְמְאוּ — דּוֹרְכָן פָּחוֹת פָּחוֹת מִכְּבֵיצָה!
phrases.english: Grapes that became impure — one presses them less than an egg-size at a time!
phrases.notes: Less than a כביצה cannot pass on impurity to the juice.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי, וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to examine the grape ruling quoted in step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that impure grapes pressed before הקדש give pure wine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling has no limit on amount, but רבי יוחנן elsewhere requires pressing less than a כביצה at a time

steps.title: First answer: here too it means less than a כביצה
steps.stepSummary: The first answer is that רבי יוחנן's ruling here also means pressing less than a כביצה at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: here too it means less than an egg-size at a time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first, simple answer to the contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two rulings do not argue. The grape ruling just did not spell out the amount, and it relies on the other ruling that limits pressing to less than a כביצה.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say — introduces one possible answer
Here too

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
Here too, it means less than an egg-size at a time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָכָא נָמֵי פָּחוֹת פָּחוֹת מִכְּבֵיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the unstated ruling assumes the same small-amount condition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The grape ruling allows pressing any amount
steps.terutzMaskana: Both rulings require pressing less than a כביצה at a time

steps.title: Second answer: different levels of impurity
steps.stepSummary: The second answer is that the two rulings deal with different levels of impurity. Grapes that are a שני need the less-than-כביצה rule. Grapes that are a שלישי do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say: there, the grapes touched a ראשון, so they became a שני. Here, they touched a שני, so they became a שלישי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer that explains why each ruling of רבי יוחנן is correct in its own case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grapes that are a שני can make liquid impure by rabbinic law, so the juice must not touch a full כביצה of grapes. Grapes that are only a שלישי cannot make the juice impure at all. That is why they may be pressed in any amount.

keyTerms.meaning: First-degree impurity
Second-degree impurity
Third-degree impurity
They touched

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's two rulings fit together. Either both require less than a כביצה, or the strict rule is for grapes that are a שני and the lenient rule is for grapes that are a שלישי.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
There, it is where they touched a first-degree impurity,
so that they themselves became second-degree.
phrases.notes: A שני can make liquid impure by rabbinic law, so the juice needs protection.

phrases.english: Here, it is where they touched a second-degree impurity,
so that they became third-degree.
phrases.notes: A שלישי does not make the juice impure, so any amount may be pressed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָתָם דְּנָגְעוּ לְהוּ בְּרִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different answer to the contradiction in step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by level of impurity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings deal with the same kind of impure grapes and contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: The small-amount rule is for grapes that are a שני. Any amount may be pressed when the grapes are a שלישי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The two rulings of רבי יוחנן do not contradict each other.

steps.title: רבא brings support from the flowing water of the red heifer
steps.stepSummary: רבא says we also learned this, from the פסוק about מים חיים: the water must flow directly into the vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We have also learned this. The פסוק says, 'And he shall put flowing water into a vessel.' This teaches that the water must flow straight into the vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a proof from a ברייתא about the water mixed with the פרה אדומה ashes. He is setting up an argument; the next step raises a difficulty in the verse, and its resolution continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads אל כלי closely. The water's 'flowing' must happen right into the vessel, so the water is still connected to its spring as it enters. This detail is what רבא will build on.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it (a source that supports the point)
Flowing (living) spring water
Their 'living' state, meaning their flowing
Vessel

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא:
phrases.english: Rava said: We too have learned it:
"And he shall put upon it flowing water
phrases.notes: במדבר יט:יז, about the ashes of the פרה אדומה

phrases.english: into a vessel" —
that their flowing should be into the vessel.
phrases.notes: The water flows straight from the source into the vessel

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא brings a source from the פרה אדומה water that supports the principle of step 10: attachment (זריעה) does not cancel the stricter status of holy things.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אושעיא's principle that זריעה (attachment to the source) does not work for הקדש, because the רבנן were stricter with holy things
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on 'מים חיים אל כלי' — the flowing must be into the vessel

steps.title: The verse seems to say the water is both detached and attached
steps.stepSummary: The word ונתן suggests the water is detached when it is put in. But the water flows straight from the spring, so it is attached.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the פסוק says 'and he shall put.' So it seems the water is detached. Yet it is attached, since it flows straight from the spring!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction inside the same פסוק. This sets up an answer that comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Putting' water sounds like taking water that is already separated and pouring it in. But אל כלי taught that the water flows straight from the spring into the vessel, so it is still connected. Both cannot be simply true, so something needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall put — sounds like pouring water that is already separated
Apparently / this shows that
Detached (separated from the source)
Attached (still connected to the source)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question against רבא. It is part of רבא's own reasoning. He raises the contradiction so that its answer will prove his point.

phrases.english: "And he shall put" — apparently they are detached.
But they are attached!
phrases.notes: Because the water flows directly from the spring into the vessel

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנָתַן אַלְמָא תְּלוּשִׁין נִינְהוּ וְהָא מְחוּבָּרִין נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It sharpens רבא's reading of the פסוק by showing a tension between ונתן and אל כלי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading of the פסוק about מים חיים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ונתן implies the water is detached, while אל כלי requires it to flow straight from the source, so it is attached. The two words seem to contradict.
